text: Running models locally

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
Where the models come from

Hugging Face is the repository. Three million public models as of August 2026, and the open-weight releases from Alibaba, Google, Meta, DeepSeek, Mistral and OpenAI all land there first.



What a listing holds
A model card, a license, and the weight files. Downloads and likes are on the page, so you can see what other people use.


Open weights, not open source
The weights are published; the license is the publisher’s own. Qwen is Apache 2.0, Llama and Gemma have custom terms. Read it before commercial use.


One model, several files
The same model is posted at full size and in smaller quantized copies. Which one you download is set by what your machine can hold.

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
What pulls and runs them










What it is
What you use it for




Ollama
A CLI and a local API, with its own registry that mirrors Hugging Face
ollama pull, then one model in a terminal or behind localhost


LM Studio
A desktop app over the same engines
Browsing, downloading and trying models without a terminal


llama.cpp
The C++ engine that runs these models on ordinary hardware
What most of the above is running underneath


MLX
Apple’s array framework, with mlx-lm for text
The fastest path on Apple silicon


vLLM
A batched inference server
A queue of documents rather than a conversation





Ollama will also pull straight from a Hugging Face repository: ollama run hf.co/user/repo.

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
Two numbers

A model is a few billion numbers. At full size each takes two bytes. Quantizing rounds them to one of sixteen levels, with a scale factor kept for each small block — a quarter of the space, and a little accuracy. A billion parameters comes to a bit over half a gigabyte.



Memory decides whether it loads
All of it has to be in memory at once, with room left over for the conversation. 30 billion parameters is 17 GB; 671 billion is about 400 GB.


Bandwidth decides how fast it generates
Bandwidth is how many gigabytes a second the chip reads from its own memory. Each token — roughly a word — costs one full read of the weights in use.
tokens/sec ≤ bandwidth ÷ active bytes

Unified memory is why these hold models a discrete card cannot: the GPU reads system RAM, so the capacity is the machine’s memory. An RTX 5090 has six times the Mac mini’s bandwidth but only 32 GB of memory.

title: Generative AI for Finance
section: Why a 30B model generates like a 3B one
text:
Why a 30B model generates like a 3B one

Both of these are mixture-of-experts models: all the weights sit in memory, and each token reads a fraction of them.



Memory holds the whole model — 17 GB for Qwen3-30B-A3B, about 400 GB for DeepSeek 671B.
A router picks 8 experts out of 128 for each token.
The read is 3.3B parameters, not 30B, so the ceiling is set by the active share.



A ceiling, not a measurement. Real throughput runs 60 to 80 percent of it, and falls as the context fills.

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
Two tasks, three models


Tell Claude

Get a key at openrouter.ai. Send each of these to all three models. Print every answer with its cost and tokens per second.



The code
Write a Python function that redacts US phone numbers, Social Security numbers and email addresses from a string, one regex per type, and returns the redacted text with a count of each.


The memo
Write 150 words to the audit committee: why client records are not going to a hosted model, and what the business gives up by that decision. The reader is a director with no technical background.

title: Generative AI for Finance
text: Security

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
Three risks

Sending data to an LLM → risks of training on your data and data breach
Letting an agent read unverified sources → risk of prompt injection
If the agent can also reach data → risk of data exfiltration

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
Where a prompt goes
Every call leaves copies. Your agreement with the provider sets how long each one is kept.


Your app
The conversation history your own code keeps so the next turn has context.


Your gateway log
Who asked, which model, how many tokens — and, if you log bodies, the prompt itself.


The provider
Held for a period set by your agreement, and separately for abuse monitoring.


Subprocessors
The hosting and infrastructure vendors listed in the provider’s data processing agreement.

title: Generative AI for Finance
section: The answer to the first risk
text:
The answer to the first risk
For almost every business use, the answer is to sign a contract and send the data. A no-train, zero-retention Data Processing Agreement — plus a BAA for PHI — comes with the standard commercial API account.









Step
What it adds
Enough for




Opt out of training (a setting; API default)
The provider will not train on it. A setting in the terms of service, revocable, and the data is still retained briefly
Personal, non-sensitive work


+ Signed DPA (+ BAA for PHI)
A contract: liability, breach notice, audit, subprocessor list
Client data, regulated data, PHI


+ Enterprise agreement
SLAs, support, indemnification, capacity, SSO
Scale and operations, not stronger privacy





Anthropic’s Data Processing Addendum.

title: Generative AI for Finance
section: Run the model in your own cloud
text:
Run the model in your own cloud
If your data is already in AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud, run the model on that same cloud.





AWS
Google Cloud
Azure




Claude
Bedrock
Vertex AI
Azure AI Foundry


GPT
Bedrock

Azure AI Foundry


Gemini

Native






The model runs inside your cloud, so the data stays in that perimeter and the model provider is not a separate party to it. It is covered by the cloud DPA and BAA you already signed, and by the cloud’s attestations — FedRAMP, SOC 2, ISO 27001.

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
HIPAA and SEC


HIPAA — a BAA is required
Satisfactory assurances “must be documented through a written contract … that meets the applicable requirements of § 164.504(e).”
45 CFR 164.502(e)


SEC Reg S-P — oversee the vendor
Written policies “reasonably designed to require oversight, including through due diligence and monitoring, of service providers.”
17 CFR 248.30

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
Beyond the contract
The DPA is a contractual guarantee, backed by liability. It is not a physical one: the data still travels to the provider. For more sensitive data, add a physical layer.


Send less — the schema, and a few synthetic rows.
De-identify — take the names out before the data reaches the context.
Run a local model — the data never leaves your environment.



Steps 2 and 3 are the rest of this session.

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
What are prompt injections?


The mechanism

Hidden instructions embedded in data — emails, documents, web pages
The LLM reads the hidden text and follows the attacker’s instructions instead of the user’s
It cannot distinguish instructions from content; it is all text


The exposure

Any agent that reads untrusted content and has access to private data or tools
The attacker needs no credentials — only a way to get text in front of the LLM
OWASP ranks prompt injection as the #1 risk for LLM applications (2025)

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
Why agents are more exposed

A tool result re-enters the context as text, in the same stream as your question.



What you typed
“Summarize the overdue invoices.”


What a tool returned
A row, a web page, an email body — whatever was in the source, verbatim.


What the model sees
One sequence of tokens. There is no field marking which part you wrote.

title: Generative AI for Finance
section: EchoLeak: Zero-click data theft from Microsoft 365 Copilot
text:
EchoLeak: Zero-click data theft from Microsoft 365 Copilot


CVE-2025-32711 — June 2025



The attacker sends the victim an email containing hidden instructions, invisible to a human reader.
The victim asks Copilot to summarize their email. Copilot reads the hidden instructions.
Following them, Copilot embeds confidential data in a URL in its response.
The victim’s browser requests that URL, sending the data to the attacker’s server.
The attacker reads the data out of the URL. Zero clicks, and nothing visible to the victim.




Copilot reads untrusted content, has access to private data, and can render URLs. All three in one LLM.

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
Three legs for data exfiltration

All three of these must be present for prompt injections to cause data exfiltration.



1. Private data
Secrets worth stealing — client records, financials, your inbox


2. Untrusted content
Attacker-controllable text — web pages, emails, uploaded files


3. An outbound channel
A way to send data out — web fetch, send email, write to a shared place

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
What follows from this


The leg you control
You cannot stop a model from reading instructions in its input, and you cannot always choose what a tool returns.
You decide how much of your data is in the context.


The other two
Untrusted content and the outbound channel are closed with containers and egress rules, when we build agents.
A local model does not close them: the machine still has a network.

title: Generative AI for Finance
text: De-identifying tables

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
Four kinds of field









Kind
Examples
What you do with it




Direct identifiers
Name, SSN, account number, email, phone
Suppress. Each one names a person on its own


Quasi-identifiers
ZIP, birth date, sex, job title, dates of service
Generalize. Identifying in combination, not alone


Sensitive attributes
Diagnosis, salary, balance, the text of a complaint
Keep. What you are protecting, and usually what the model needs


Everything else
Product code, region, quantity
Keep. Carries nobody’s identity

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
The HIPAA safe harbor
Eighteen identifiers come out, in nine groups. Remove all of them, and have no actual knowledge that what remains could identify someone, and the data is no longer PHI — no business associate agreement required.








Group
What comes out




Names
The individual’s, and those of relatives, employers, and household members


Geography
Everything below the state, except the first three ZIP digits where that area holds more than 20,000 people


Dates
Every element but the year. Ages above 89 become “90 or older”


Contact
Telephone, fax, email


Numbers
SSN, medical record, health plan, account, certificate, license


Device and vehicle
Serial numbers, VINs, license plates


Online
URLs, IP addresses


Biometric and images
Finger and voice prints, full-face photographs


Catch-all
Any other unique identifying number, characteristic, or code

title: Generative AI for Finance
section: Two HIPAA routes, and two GDPR terms
text:
Two HIPAA routes, and two GDPR terms


HIPAA

Safe harbor — remove the eighteen. Mechanical and auditable, and it discards data you may need
Expert determination — a qualified statistician certifies that the risk of re-identification is very small, and documents the method. Keeps more of the data


GDPR

Anonymized data falls outside the Regulation
Pseudonymized data is still personal data and still in scope. Replacing a name with a token does not make the data anonymous, because you hold the mapping



45 CFR 164.514(b)(1) and (b)(2); GDPR Article 4(5) and Recital 26.

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
The techniques










What it does
What survives




Suppress
Drop the field
Nothing of it


Mask
Keep the shape, drop the content: XXX-XX-4312
The format


Pseudonymize
One stable surrogate key per person
Joins, and counts per person


Generalize
34 → 30–39; 77005 → 770; a date → its month
The distribution, at lower resolution


Perturb
Add noise to amounts and dates
Totals and trends, not single rows


Aggregate
Group totals, with a minimum cell size
Comparisons between groups


Synthesize
Rows with the same schema and distributions
The distributions, no real person’s data


Schema only
Column names and types, no rows
Enough to write a query

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
No model is involved
Every row in that table is arithmetic or a lookup. It runs on your machine, in code you can read.
df["customer_id"] = df["customer"].map(surrogate)   # from your own table
df["zip3"]        = df["zip"].str[:3]
df["month"]       = df["order_date"].dt.to_period("M")
df = df.drop(columns=["customer", "email", "phone", "zip", "order_date"])

df.groupby(["zip3", "month"]).size().min()          # the smallest group

pandas for the transforms, Faker for synthetic values, and ARX or sdcMicro when you need a certified k-anonymity report.

title: Generative AI for Finance
section: Three properties of doing it in code
text:
Three properties of doing it in code


Deterministic — the same row always produces the same output, so you can write a test for it.
Auditable — the rule for each column is a line of code you can show a regulator.
Local — nothing is sent anywhere to decide what to remove, and the removal happens before anything leaves.

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
Re-identification


Massachusetts, 1997
The state released hospital discharge records for state employees with names and addresses removed. Latanya Sweeney bought the Cambridge voter roll for $20, matched on ZIP, birth date and sex, and found the governor’s records.


Netflix, 2008
Netflix released 100 million ratings from 480,000 subscribers, user IDs replaced by numbers. Narayanan and Shmatikov matched them against public IMDb reviews and named individual subscribers.



ZIP, birth date and sex identify 87 percent of the US population uniquely (Sweeney, 2000). The direct identifiers were gone in both of these cases.

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
A test you can run

Group the rows by the quasi-identifiers you are about to send. Count each group.



k-anonymity — no group smaller than k, so every record looks like at least k−1 others. Where a group is too small, generalize further or drop it
l-diversity — within a group, the sensitive attribute has to vary. If five records match on ZIP and month and all carry the same diagnosis, the diagnosis is known for all five

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
Pseudonymize out, re-identify in



Your code


Replaces each person with a surrogate key. The mapping table stays in your database.




The model


Sees CUSTOMER_0417 and the figures. Reasons over them, writes, returns.




Your code again


Reads the mapping back and puts the names in before anyone sees the output.




The model never holds the mapping, so nothing it emits — including anything an injected instruction makes it emit — carries a name.

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
Where it has to happen


In code, before the call
A system prompt telling the model to ignore the names does nothing about the names you sent.


Before your own log
The gateway logs prompts and completions. That log is a second copy of whatever you sent.


Not by the model doing the work
A model asked to redact a document has already read it.

title: Generative AI for Finance
text: De-identifying text

title: Generative AI for Finance
section: A table and a notes field
text:
A table and a notes field


A table
The identifiers are in named columns. You decide once per column, and the decision holds for every row.

Free text
A notes field, an email body, a scanned PDF. The name is in the middle of a sentence, and so are the place, the quantity and the date.

title: Generative AI for Finance
section: Why this job needs the local model
text:
Why this job needs the local model


The reason
A scrubber has to read the raw text. Sending it to a hosted model to decide what to remove sends the unscrubbed text.
The weights sit on your disk, so the unscrubbed document stays on your machine.


The size
Span tagging: find the name, return a label. The open models used for this run 4B to 12B parameters, under 7 GB on disk at 4-bit.
Choose by the recall you measure on your own sample.

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
Three tools, in order



Regex


SSNs, account numbers, phone numbers, emails — anything with a format you can write down. Exact and free, and it finds every string matching the pattern you wrote.




A named-entity scrubber


Microsoft Presidio, spaCy. A purpose-built NER model, not a general LLM: it tags people, places, organizations and dates, and hands back spans to replace.




A local LLM


The last pass, over what the first two left. It reads the sentence, so it catches the identifier that is identifying only in context.




The first two passes are deterministic and testable, so they run before the LLM.

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
Why the LLM goes last


It is not deterministic
The same paragraph twice can come back scrubbed two different ways. You cannot write a test that keeps passing.


It has no recall guarantee
Regex finds every string matching the pattern. An LLM finds most of them, and you do not know which it missed.


It can invent
Asked to replace a name, it may also rewrite the clause around it. Check that the rest of the text is unchanged.

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
Measuring the scrubber
No scrubber catches everything, so measure how much it misses.


Take a sample of documents and mark the identifiers by hand.
Run the pipeline over the same sample.
Count what it missed and what it removed that it should have kept.
Write both numbers down, with the date and the model, next to the decision to accept them.



Recall is the number an auditor asks for.

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
What de-identification does not do


It does not replace the contract
Your DPA and your vendor-oversight obligations apply to any vendor you use, whatever you send them.


It does not cover the agent’s tools
If a tool reaches the raw table, what you scrubbed out of the prompt is back in the context.


It is not free
A generalized ZIP cannot be geocoded; a perturbed amount cannot be reconciled. Decide what the answer needs first.

text: Exercises

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
De-identify a table
Take a table with customers in it — a brokerage account table with names, addresses and balances will do. Ask Claude to generate one if you do not have one.


Tell Claude

Write a function deidentify(df) for this table. Suppress the direct identifiers. Replace the customer with a stable surrogate key, and keep the mapping table in a separate file. Generalize the postal code to three characters and the order date to its month. Then report the size of the smallest group under postal code + month.

Run it, read what is left, and ask whether you could still pick someone out of it.

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
A local chatbot


Install Ollama: ollama.com/download.
In a terminal, type ollama run gemma4:e2b-it-qat. The download is 4.3 GB.
Ask it something you asked a frontier model. Compare the two answers.
Type /bye to leave. Then run ollama run gemma3:1b, an 815 MB download from the previous generation, and ask the same question again.



Nothing you type leaves your machine. In a second terminal window, ollama ps shows what is loaded and how much memory it holds.

title: Generative AI for Finance
section: Scrub text with the local model
text:
Scrub text with the local model
Write four or five customer complaints with names, places and dates in them.


Run a regex pass for the formats you can specify, and see what is left.
Send the remainder to the local model from the last exercise, asking it to replace each person with a label and each place with its region.
Run the same text through twice. Compare the two outputs.
Count what it missed.



Step 3 shows whether the model is deterministic; step 4 is its recall.

Instructions that are always read (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md)

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
CLAUDE.md



At the start of each conversation, Claude looks in specific places for CLAUDE.md files
It looks in your home directory (C:\users\yourname on Windows) and it looks in the project folder




A CLAUDE.md is a text file that contains instructions for Claude
Claude reads the entire file, so use it sparingly




You could get the same behavior by pasting the instructions in the prompt window. OpenAI calls the file AGENTS.md; Google reads either AGENTS.md or GEMINI.md.

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
The equivalent in each tool








Tool
Where standing instructions live




Chat and Cowork
Settings → General → Instructions for Claude, plus instructions on each project


Code — Local
CLAUDE.md files on your hard drive


Code CLI
the same CLAUDE.md files





Cowork keeps its instructions in the app, not in files — global in Settings, per-project in the project panel, per-folder in a text box on the folder you select. Chat reads only what you upload or add to a project, so its standing instructions live in the settings rather than in a file.

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
Example: Keep things organized

Handoff (summary) docs, AI outputs, and scripts proliferate over time
To reduce the amount of reading (and tokens) AI must do to locate things, have Claude keep a map of what each file is and what it draws on



In CLAUDE.md — one line

Read MAP.md at the start of every session to get oriented in this folder.


Building and rebuilding the map is a skill, not a CLAUDE.md rule. We will get to that.

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
Chat and Cowork


Account-wide
Settings → Instructions for Claude. Read at the start of every conversation and every scheduled task.


One project
A project carries its own instructions alongside its folders and links. Cowork projects live on your computer; Chat projects live in your Claude account.


Project memory
A Cowork project also keeps a memory store. Claude writes to it during a session and reads it back the next time.

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
Where Code looks for CLAUDE.md
Loaded in this order — broadest first, most specific last:


A managed file installed by IT, applying to everyone on the machine
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md — applies to you in every project
CLAUDE.md or .claude/CLAUDE.md in the project folder — checked into git and shared with the team
CLAUDE.local.md in the project folder — yours alone, kept out of git



/init drafts one from your folder, # at the start of a prompt appends a line, and /memory opens the files for editing. A folder with an AGENTS.md and no CLAUDE.md is read the same way.

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
Skills


At the start of each conversation, Claude also looks in specific places for SKILL.md files


It looks in your home directory (C:\users\yourname on Windows) and it looks in the project folder




Skills are text files saved on your hard drive. Claude reads the top of each SKILL.md file (the skill description) on startup, and it reads the bulk of the file only when needed

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
Anthropic skills
Anthropic publishes its own skills at https://github.com/anthropics/skills
Pre-installed on claude.ai and Claude Desktop


xlsx
Excel workbooks


docx
Word documents


pptx
PowerPoint decks


pdf
PDF files

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
Invoking skills


Slash Command

Type /skillname at the prompt
Example: /plan
Invokes the skill directly



Natural Language

Describe what you need in plain English
Example: “Use your planning mode and evaluate …”



Automatic

Claude may invoke a skill on its own
Example: “Create an Excel file” triggers the xlsx skill automatically
Driven by the skill’s description

title: Generative AI for Finance
section: Adding a skill in Claude Desktop
text:
Adding a skill in Claude Desktop
Skills are saved prompts for specific tasks — reusable workflows you can share with your team.



Click Customize in the left sidebar
Select Skills
Click + → Create skill → Upload a skill
Drag and drop or browse to a SKILL.md file

Works the same in Chat, Cowork, and Code modes. In Cowork and Code, you can tell Claude to create and save the skill.

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
Creating skills



Usual process is you work on something, iterating until you get what you want.




You realize you may want the same thing again, and you don’t want to go through the iteration again.




Solution: tell Claude to package the final version as a skill.

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
Example 1


Tell Claude to create a skill for your folder named “pirate” with this content: “Always answer like a pirate” (On Claude Desktop: Customize/Skills/Add/Create a skill).


Start a new conversation. Enter /pirate What is the meaning of life?

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
Example 2


Ask Claude to add one line to your project CLAUDE.md: read MAP.md at the start of every session
Tell Claude to create an update-map skill that scans the folder and writes MAP.md as a table — file, what it is, what it draws on — creating the file if there isn’t one
Start a new conversation and enter /update-map. Open MAP.md and read it
Add a file to the folder, run /update-map again, and find the new entry



The skill writes the map on its first run, so there is nothing to set up before you invoke it. The CLAUDE.md line takes effect in the next conversation, not the one you are in.

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
Example 3
critique: skill I wrote to review work Claude has produced — a draft, a deck, or code.


Launches reviewer agents in parallel: correctness traced back to the source files, clarity, and a devil’s advocate that reads the code
Argues against every finding and keeps only the ones that survive
Publishes an HTML page with the findings and the options for what to do next



Invoked with /critique. It runs several subagents, so it takes longer and uses more tokens than most skills.

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
Plugins
A shipping protocol for skills plus scripts, MCP connectors, and other files

Visit the Anthropic plugin directory: Enter /plugin as a Claude prompt or visit https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official



Thousands of people (including your prof) have created their own plugin marketplaces. Everything is free.


The most useful things will be the ones you create (with Claude’s assistance)

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
Example: Anthropic’s Data plugin

What it adds
Six commands — /analyze, /explore-data, /write-query, /create-viz, /build-dashboard, /validate-data — against any SQL database with an MCP server, or an uploaded CSV

/plugin marketplace add anthropics/knowledge-work-plugins then /plugin install data@knowledge-work-plugins

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
What the plugin adds
A checklist with named failure modes, each with how to detect it and how to prevent it:








Pitfall
What goes wrong




Join explosion
A many-to-many join multiplies rows and inflates every count and sum


Survivorship bias
Only the entities that still exist are in the data; the churned ones are missing


Incomplete period
A partial month compared against a full one


Denominator shifting
“Eligible” or “active” was redefined between the periods being compared


Average of averages
Group averages averaged together when the groups are different sizes


Timezone mismatch
One source on UTC, another on local time, rolled up at different cutoffs


Selection bias
The segment is defined by the outcome being measured





Plus Simpson’s paradox, a QA checklist covering data quality, calculation, reasonableness and presentation, and a verdict of ready to share, share with caveats, or needs revision.

text:

text: How large language models work

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
Tokenization
Text is cut into pieces from a fixed vocabulary before the model sees any of it.
"The cat sat on the mat"  ->  ["The", " cat", " sat", " on", " the", " mat"]

"Unbelievable"            ->  ["Un", "believ", "able"]
Common words stay whole; rare and long words break into pieces. A typical vocabulary runs to about 100,000 tokens.

Numbers break on the same rules, which have nothing to do with arithmetic. 13,963,378.65 reaches the model as a handful of unrelated pieces.

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
Vectors
Each token is associated with a vector, meaning a list of numbers. So, a sequence of text becomes a sequence of lists of numbers.


Each token is a list
“king” becomes a list of 4,096 numbers. “queen” becomes a different but somewhat similar list of 4,096 numbers.
Tokens used in similar contexts end up near each other.


The space is mostly empty
There are far more possible vectors than there are tokens, so most points in the space name nothing.
The prediction can land between tokens. The “closest” token is usually selected but not always (so LLM output is somewhat random).

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
The whole task

Given the tokens (lists of numbers) so far, predict the token (list of numbers) that comes next. That is the entire operation.

Everything a model appears to do — answering, summarizing, writing code, refusing — is that one prediction, repeated.

📝

title: Generative AI for Finance
section: A neural network is a function
text:
A neural network is a function


The idea
\(y = 4x\) is a function. The 4 is a parameter.
Change it to 3 and you have the same structure with different behavior.

The scale
Same idea with perhaps trillions of parameters, arranged as a transformer — the architecture published by Google researchers in 2017.

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
From prediction to conversation
A model trained only to predict the next token continues your text. It does not answer a question.


Role tokens. The text is wrapped in markers: <|user|> your question <|assistant|>.
Instruction tuning. The model is further trained on examples where what follows <|assistant|> is a useful reply.
Reinforcement learning from human feedback. Raters score replies, and the model is trained toward what raters preferred.


The mechanism did not change. What changed is which continuation is the likely one. GPT became Chat-GPT in 2022.

title: Generative AI for Finance
text: Effective use of AI

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
Managing conversations


Start a new conversation for a new task
AI reads the entire conversation (the context window) each time you prompt. Irrelevant stuff consumes tokens and may be confusing.


When a conversation gets long
Tell AI to write a handoff document so you can start a fresh conversation. How long? There is a tradeoff; it depends on how much is irrelevant.

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
Good enough prompting

Most ‘prompt engineering’ techniques from a few years ago are now either useless or actually counterproductive. Don’t tell it “you are an expert data scientist” or “think step by step.”



Tell it what you want, not what to do
I want … How can we do it?


Ask AI for help in prompting
If you are unsure how to ask something, ask AI how to ask it.


If something doesn’t work
Try again.



Treat AI as an infinitely patient colleague with a poor memory.

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
Plan, evaluate, critique


Your go-to prompt
Think about the best way to do this, and let’s develop a plan together.


Ex-post diagnosis
Prompt: Explain what you did step by step. Did you make any decisions that we have not discussed? Write this as an HTML doc.


Use AI to evaluate
Start a new conversation or ask for a subagent. Ask it to evaluate the first agent’s work, summarized in the HTML doc, relative to your goals.

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
What this buys

AI is a prediction machine. Ask it to do something, and it will probably do what it has seen most often in its training data.
Ask it the best way to do something, and it will regurgitate evaluations of methods it has seen.
Ask it to proceed after explaining the best way, it will read the “the best way is …” in the conversation history and follow that.

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
Misunderstandings and unstated assumptions are the most common sources of errors. Discuss before and after to surface those.
AI is not good at critiquing itself in the same conversation, because it reads its reasoning in the conversation history and predicts the same thing. You need a fresh context window to get a reliable critique.

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
Numbers need code
If a number appears and no code produced it, it was predicted. Do this instead.


Prompt

Compute this in Python. Do not report a number you did not compute with code.

Asked to sum three numbers 83, 16, 104, AI is much better at predicting the code sum([83, 16, 104]) than it is at predicting what should follow 83 + 16 + 104 =

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
Hallucinations

AI predicts text. It does not check what it produces against a source.

Hallucinations are most likely when it is asked to recall something specific that is not in front of it:

Citations, quotes, and URLs
Numbers about a particular company, year, or dataset
Options and arguments of niche or recent software


Verify the facts
Ask for a source and look it up.

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
Hallucinations in code


Caught by running it
A made-up function or argument raises an error as soon as the code runs. The agent reads the traceback and fixes it.


Not caught by running it
The wrong column, a join that drops rows, a filter on the wrong year. The code runs and returns a number.



The second kind is a misunderstanding or an unstated assumption, not a hallucination. Discussing the plan beforehand and the decisions afterwards is what surfaces it.

text: Claude and Excel

title: Generative AI for Finance
text:
How Claude builds a workbook


Creating a workbook
Claude writes Python — the openpyxl library — that loops over every cell and inserts data, formulas, and formatting.


Editing a workbook
To edit a workbook, Claude reads the XML and edits it. An .xlsx unzips into one XML file per worksheet, with the text in sharedStrings.xml and the formatting in styles.xml; each cell is an element holding a value or a formula. Claude rewrites those elements and repacks the file, so charts, pivot tables, and formatting it did not touch are unchanged.



The formulas are live. A workbook Claude builds opens in Excel as a model you can change.

text:

If your organization blocks the Office Store, IT deploys it instead through the Microsoft 365 Admin Center
Sign in to your Claude account when prompted
